propositions: The gate matches field names globally using bare attribute name membership, so a field is incorrectly satisfied when any unrelated config declares an attribute with the same name, even if the field itself is never read.
The defect is a false-negative class affecting common field names (enabled, path, timeout, remote, branch, mode) that are reused across configs and therefore masked by this resolution flaw.

Receiver resolution must bind attribute reads to their owning dataclass through six patterns: section-attribute names, annotations, alias assignments, return types, conditional branches, and cross-module parameter bindings from call sites.

Four fields (McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, JiraConfig.allow_insecure) are newly flagged by the corrected gate; each has a real consumer via excluded plumbing files or string-key reads, and receives a factual # read-via: marker.

Existing test files must migrate from the obsolete bare-name contract to the owner-resolution contract, including inverting test_unrelated_same_named_attribute_keeps_the_gate_quiet to expect a firing.

The fixed gate reports any # read-via: marker whose pointer names a rebar ticket id (indicating a marker parked against a since-closed ticket), and includes RED-first proof via a frozen pre-fix snapshot to prevent regression to bare-name matching.
